name: Trigeminal Neuralgia
definition: Recurrent unilateral brief electric shock-like facial pain limited to one or more divisions of the trigeminal nerve, triggered by innocuous stimuli in classical presentations.

typical: Trigger zones with touch, chewing, talking or brushing teeth
Neurological exam is usually normal in classical TN

redFlags.item: Sensory loss or other cranial nerve deficit
Persistent background pain with systemic features
Concern for multiple sclerosis, tumour or infection

investigations.principle: Brain MRI is generally recommended to assess secondary causes and neurovascular compression in appropriate patients.
investigations.MRI: MRI with trigeminal protocol may be useful for surgical planning.

green: Patient education about triggers and treatment adherence
amber: Carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine and procedural/surgical options require interaction, laboratory and specialist review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Classical Ayurvedic one-to-one equivalence should not be assumed; facial Vata-neuralgia phenotype may be documented separately.

patientEducation.summary: Recurrent unilateral brief electric shock-like facial pain limited to one or more divisions of the trigeminal nerve, triggered by innocuous stimuli in classical presentations.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.

sources.title: Guidelines for management of trigeminal neuralgia
